title: Every measurement shares one remembered look, blue by default, and any change to a caliper becomes the new default
goal: Size, Gap and Distance measurements all wear the same look: by default a calm blue to blue grey set (dark navy readout chip with a blue ring and white number, blue caliper lines, and for Size a faint blue box over the measured area), like the user's screenshot. Changing the colour or look of any caliper, including the width or height caliper inside a Size group, makes that the look every new measurement in any mode starts with. There is no separate Size versus Gap colour.
notes:
User's words (2026-10-13): "when i make a size measurement and change the colors used for the calipers, it doesn't seem to remember the next time I use it. I'd like the defaults for all measurements to be shades of bluish to bluish grey and all match. like this [screenshot]. But if i change either caliper in the size group, it remembers for all new calipers used in measurement tools. gap vs size shouldn't be different for example." Screenshot 2026-10-13 06.54.34: calipers with dark navy pill chips, blue ring, white '19 px', '48 px', '174 px', thin blue lines, and a faint blue box over 'edited'.

This REVERSES two earlier choices: the per-role colours (Size red, Spacing blue: PhotonzCore/MeasureStyles.swift ~:90-110 role, sizeColors, spacingColors; content(for role:) :297) and the red 10% Size box from a-size-measurement-is-one-group-a-faint-red-box (now blue, matching). Remembering: EditorState+MeasurePanel.swift rememberMeasureColors(of:) (:283) and updateMeasureStyles (:295), persisted in UserDefaults measureStylesKey; addElementSize (EditorState+Measure.swift:97) reads measureStyles.content(for: .size). Related done: measurements-are-named-for-their-mode-and-every (same appearance controls for all calipers).
acceptance: Reproduce first at Next defaults: make a Size measurement, change its width caliper's line and chip colours (through the panel), make another Size and a Gap; record which colours each new one took and why the change was not remembered (suspect: edits on a caliper inside the Size group do not reach rememberMeasureColors / MeasureStyles.absorb)

One shared remembered look for all measurement modes: MeasureStyles keeps one set of colours (line, chip fill, chip ring, text) and the Size box tint; the per-role sizeColors/spacingColors split stops deciding a new caliper's colours (the Role control, if it stays, never changes colours); existing remembered per-role styles migrate to the shared one using the last edited set

New defaults (for anyone who has not tuned them, and for the shipped Size and Spacing styles in the Library): taken from the user's screenshot (Screenshot 2026-10-13 at 06.54.34): chip fill dark navy (about #23345A), chip ring and caliper line mid blue (about #4D7FD6), number white, Size box tint the same blue at 10% (replacing yesterday's red); exact values chosen by sampling the screenshot and written in the audit; legible on light and dark pictures (checked on both)

Any colour or look change on any caliper (Size width or height inside the group, a Gap, a Distance, the Size box's tint) updates the shared remembered look at once, so the next measurement in ANY mode starts with it; MEASURED by a walk
Old documents' measurements keep the colours they were drawn with

A walk changes the Size group's width caliper line to green, then makes a Gap and a Distance and checks both start green; resets, and checks a fresh install's first Size, Gap and Distance are the blue set
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.
